Dependable finance candidate with 10+ years of experience (his: "6 years")

expert_defects.cause: lib/resume/tailor/optimizer.js:232 computes years = experienceSpanYears(base) (first start date of any role → today) and prints it at :256; lib/resume/tailor/tailor.js:102 does the same for the fallback summary.
expert_defects.fix: Count only roles in the target family, never exceed a number the résumé states itself, and leave the number out when unsure.

expert_defects.title: Interview Prep's spoken intro and answers get tenure and employers wrong, and the guard can't catch it

examples.text: the last three and a half [years] as an Assistant Store Manager at Desert Sun Apparel (dates: Apr 2021 – present = 5.5)
almost four years of experience at St. Aurelia Medical Center (dates: Aug 2020 – present = 6.2)

expert_defects.cause: lib/server/interviewPrep.js prepPrompt (:221) gives the model neither today's date nor per-role tenure, so it does date arithmetic itself. guardPack checks only digit tokens (NUM_RE :145, numbersBacked), so number words ("four", "sixty to seventy") pass, and nothing checks that a story is told about the employer of its resume_fact.
expert_defects.fix: Put today's date and the computed tenure of each role in the prompt. Normalise number words before numbersBacked. Reject an answer that names a different employer from its resume_fact's role.

35 — Requires a Bachelor's degree; your résumé lists no degree (B.B.A., Accounting)

Requires a high school diploma; your résumé lists no degree (B.A., Communication)

expert_defects.cause: lib/optimizer/extractResumeFacts.js:41 DEGREE_RE ends "b\.a\." with \b, which never matches before ",", a space or end of line, and it has no B.B.A. lib/optimizer/constraints.js:101 checks a certification with hasStemmed(text, "RN license") — a literal phrase with no synonyms.
expert_defects.fix: End dotted degrees with (?=[\s,;)]|$) and add B.B.A./BSN. Match licenses by acronym and synonym (RN ⇐ "RN", "Registered Nurse"; Food Handler ⇐ "ServSafe Food Handler"; forklift certification ⇐ "Forklift / Reach Truck certification").

hit rate every week of the season → hit rate e week of the season.

with every family → with e family

expert_defects.fix: Always prefix the pattern with (?<![A-Za-z-]). Add a regression test with "every".

expert_defects.title: HumanProof / Human Voice breaks every message it touches and improves nothing

examples.text: …lines up directly with what the role calls for. → …with what the role calls.

expert_defects.fix: Run tidy only at removal sites. Treat the job title and company as evidence. Match metrics with \b…\b.

my hands-on experience with pay and charlotte

expert_defects.fix: Rank only the requirement and responsibility sections (reuse parseSections in lib/server/jobInsights.js) and only dictionary skills. Never use the employer's industry words (clinics, patients) as the candidate's work.

output.day_30:
First 30 days — Learn and earn trust:
• Meet your manager, peers, and your store or district manager, the department leads, and the associates you schedule and coach; document how success is measured for this Store Manager.
• Get hands-on with the store's sales, labor and shrink reports, the schedule, and the inventory system tied to P&L.

output.day_60:

• Take ownership of work centred on P&L and hiring and team development.

output.day_90:

• Bring a point of view on retail — a recommendation backed by what you've learned.
• Set goals with your manager for the next quarter so you're seen as someone who compounds.

output.cover_letter_framework:

output.referral_strategy: Find 1–2 people at Northgate Distribution through LinkedIn (filter by company + your school or past employers). output.opening_note: A 30/60/90 plan you can attach or bring to the interview — it signals you already think like a Warehouse Shift Lead – 2nd Shift at Northgate Distribution, and it puts your existing strength in warehouse management system (WMS) front and centre.
output.day_30:
First 30 days — Learn and earn trust:
• Meet your manager, peers, and your lead, dispatch, and the dock/loading crew; document how success is measured for this Warehouse Shift Lead – 2nd Shift.
• Get hands-on with the scanner/WMS, pick paths, and safety procedures tied to warehouse management system (WMS).
• Hit the standard rate cleanly and log zero safety incidents. Lean on your existing strength in warehouse management system (WMS) to ramp faster than expected.
output.day_60:
Days 31–60 — Contribute independently:
• Take ownership of work centred on warehouse management system (WMS) and warehouse.
• Find one picks/hour, on-time dispatch, or error rate number you can measurably improve, and propose the change to your manager.
• Build relationships across your lead, dispatch, and the dock/loading crew so you're not working in a silo.
output.day_90:

• Deliver a result tied to warehouse management system (WMS) with a number attached (picks/hour, on-time dispatch, or error rate). Aim for a result on the scale of your past work (e.g. "Operated sit-down and stand-up forklifts and reach trucks; loaded 18–22 trailers per shift").
• Bring a point of view on forklift — a recommendation backed by what you've learned.
• Set goals with your manager for the next quarter so you're seen as someone who compounds.

output.day_30:

• Meet your manager, peers, and charge nurses, physicians, and the care team on your unit; document how success is measured for this Registered Nurse – Telemetry (Nights).

• Complete onboarding/competency checks and shadow a full shift end-to-end. Lean on your existing strength in acute care to ramp faster than expected.
output.day_60:

output.day_90:

• Bring a point of view on patient care — a recommendation backed by what you've learned.
• Set goals with your manager for the next quarter so you're seen as someone who compounds.

Assess, plan, implement and evaluate care for 4–5 telemetry patients per shift. output.cover_letter_framework:
Paragraph 1 — Hook: Name the Senior Accountant role and one specific reason Lone Star Energy Partners stands out to you (a product, value, or recent move). State that your real experience with accounting maps directly to what they need.

Paragraph 2 — Proof: Use your real result: "Own month-end close for 3 entities; cut the close from 8 to 5 business days by building a close checklist and reconciliation templates". Lead with that number. Show, don't claim.

Paragraph 3 — Close: Connect that result to the impact you'd have at Lone Star Energy Partners in this role, and ask for the conversation. Keep the whole letter under 250 words.
output.referral_strategy: Find 1–2 people at Lone Star Energy Partners through LinkedIn (filter by company + your school or past employers). output.opening_note: A 30/60/90 plan you can attach or bring to the interview — it signals you already think like a Senior Accountant at Lone Star Energy Partners, and it puts your existing strength in accounting front and centre.
output.day_30:

• Meet your manager, peers, and the controller, AP/AR, and the budget owners you support; document how success is measured for this Senior Accountant.

• Complete your first month-end tasks accurately and on time. Lean on your existing strength in accounting to ramp faster than expected.
output.day_60:

• Take ownership of work centred on accounting and GAAP.
• Find one close time, reconciliation accuracy, or invoices processed number you can measurably improve, and propose the change to your manager.
• Build relationships across the controller, AP/AR, and the budget owners you support so you're not working in a silo.
output.day_90:

• Deliver a result tied to accounting with a number attached (close time, reconciliation accuracy, or invoices processed). • Bring a point of view on ERP systems — a recommendation backed by what you've learned.
• Set goals with your manager for the next quarter so you're seen as someone who compounds.
